notes:
stoa-core review confidence: high. All 41 src files and 4 integration test files read in full (src/lib.rs, error.rs, article.rs, canonical.rs, signing.rs, validation.rs, hlc.rs, wildmat.rs, msgid_map.rs, migrations.rs, db_pool.rs, rate_limiter.rs, circuit_breaker.rs, audit.rs, telemetry.rs, injection_source.rs, secret.rs, util.rs, group_log/types.rs, append.rs, verify.rs, storage.rs, mem_storage.rs, sqlite_storage.rs, reconcile.rs, backfill.rs, storage_tests.rs, ipld/codec.rs, blocks.rs, root_node.rs, builder.rs, metadata.rs, mime.rs, header_map.rs, mime_parser.rs, cid_util.rs, test_vectors.rs, ipfs/mod.rs, ipfs_backend.rs, plus both Cargo.toml files). 6 P0, 8 P1, 6 P2, 4 P3, 4 P4 findings plus 5 decision records filed. Fuzz targets not reviewed per instructions.
auth+verify: Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — EC JWK curve/alg defaulting gap, OIDC no-timeout, AllProvidersFailed leaking error details, and missing operator-name case folding are individually minor but collectively represent multiple ways to misconfigure authentication silently.
lmdb+tls+ctl: Maintainer risk: LOW — LMDB is well-isolated with good RAII hygiene; TLS config is straightforward rustls usage; ctl is a thin CLI with no secret storage. Primary risks are mutex-poisoning brittleness in lmdb and plaintext token over HTTP in ctl when used off-loopback.
small-crates: Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — Error handling is mostly good (thiserror used where appropriate, OidcError/TlsError/LmdbError are missing source chains for some variants). Type design is clean. Main gaps: Ctx fields pub in evaluator module, ParseError missing std::error::Error impl, and several iterator/collection allocation patterns that could be leaner.
small-crates: Confidence: 80% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: (1) no live cross-validation between sieve-native :matches capture and a third-party Sieve implementation beyond the stoa-sieve oracle for the address/envelope capture gap; (2) DKIM verification correctness depends on mail-auth internals (header canonicalization, signature scope) which were not traced into; (3) x_sig sign/verify round-trip tests are the only coverage for the excision logic -- no external signing tool vector confirms byte-exact excision.
RISK: P0 findings (not counting prior session P0s): (1) stat_article <msgid> always 430 never 223 (stoa-z985k); (2) Tantivy commit confirmed wired — closed. No new auth-bypass P0s found beyond those already filed (zmn9.23, zmn9.25, zmn9.29, zmn9.33). New P0 count this session: 1 (stoa-z985k). P1 security findings: check_bearer_token length leak (already stoa-ftx6h.6), XGET no TLS/auth gate (stoa-p8thp), smtp_relay UTF-8 lossy (stoa-24j77), KuboBlockStore CID mismatch (stoa-aam43), log_append debug_assert (stoa-ed8st). Overall risk: MEDIUM-HIGH. The codebase is well-structured with good test coverage but has several RFC 3977 conformance gaps and one P0 STAT correctness bug.
IDIOM RATING: 7/10. Strengths: consistent use of async_trait, tokio RwLock/Mutex, sqlx AnyPool, structured tracing, proper forbid(unsafe_code), subtle::ConstantTimeEq where needed. Weaknesses: (1) header-boundary helper duplicated 3x (injection.rs, smtp_relay.rs, post/mod.rs); (2) date parsing split between mailparse and chrono; (3) u64/i64 casts without overflow checks; (4) MemIpfsStore uses Vec<u8> key where Cid is directly hashable; (5) sep_len magic values duplicated across 4 files; (6) GroupMetadataCache O(n) eviction; (7) from_utf8_lossy in security-adjacent paths (smtp_relay, overview). No unsafe code outside allowed boundary. Error types are well-defined.
CONFIDENCE: 88%. All 55 source files and 8 test files read. Files not read this session that were in scope: none (complete). Known gaps: (1) Backend store implementations (s3_store, azure_store, gcs_store, rocks_store, pg_store, git_store, webdav_store, lmdb_store, sqlite_store, fs_store, object_store_backend) were not deeply reviewed — they implement the same IpfsBlockStore trait but may have backend-specific bugs. (2) Migration SQL files not read. (3) stoa_core, stoa_auth, stoa_smtp, stoa_verify dependencies not reviewed. The 12% uncertainty covers these areas and any emergent concurrency bugs in the lifecycle.rs dispatch flow that require end-to-end tracing to detect.
MAINTAINER RISK RATING: HIGH. The crate has 5 P0 correctness bugs that affect production behaviour: (1) IpfsLatencyMonitor completely disconnected from the pipeline — backpressure does not exist at all; (2) key-rotation articles rejected at ingress due to missing Date: header — key rotation silently broken; (3) drain_workers config field silently ignored — scaling config has no effect; (4) cmd_status active-peer count SQL condition wrong; (5) suck_pull / ingestion size limit inconsistency causing wasted fetches. Additionally there are 3 P1 correctness findings (hlc_persist node_id loss, block_cache ordering race, partial-commit IPFS+msgid without log entry), 2 P1 security findings (IPNS advisory lock leak on panic, trusted-key revocation not applied to active sessions), and 5 other P1 maintainability items. The codebase is not safe to deploy in a high-availability configuration without addressing at minimum the P0 and P1 correctness/security items.
IDIOM RATING: GOOD with targeted gaps. The codebase uses Rust 2021 idioms consistently: LazyLock for statics, impl_ipfs_store_via_inner! macro to eliminate boilerplate, subtle::ConstantTimeEq for all trusted-key comparisons, wrapping_add on counters, is_some_and, div_ceil. Notable gaps: (1) three sites use IpfsError::WriteFailed for non-write errors (FsStore::get_raw, RadosStore::delete — both P4 idiom items); (2) u64→i64 narrowing casts without TryFrom in audit_log; (3) chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp deprecated in gc_report; (4) WebDavStore manually implements IpfsStore instead of using the macro. No unsafe code outside the documented rados_store boundary.
CONFIDENCE: 88%. All 65 source files in src/ and all 13 test files in tests/ were read in full across two sessions. The workspace Cargo.toml and crates/transit/Cargo.toml were also read. The review did not include: the migrations/ and migrations_pg/ SQL files (schema correctness), the spikes/ directory, or any non-Rust configuration. Confidence deductions: (5%) the double-increment of consecutive_failures (P1) requires call-site audit of all rejection paths that was not completed — the finding is directionally correct but the exact call graph needs tracing; (7%) some config fields (e.g. AdminConfig.rate_limit_rpm) were noted as possibly unwired but the full main.rs wiring was not exhaustively traced for every field.
title: Review: entire stoa codebase
